The process takes place during the day under low light conditions but may also take place at night if there is sufficient solar energy available to meet metabolic needs. This is why some plants cannot survive without light in winter or darkness even on cloudy days.

The temperature at which a liquid boils.
Water freezes in its liquid state and turns to ice when it reaches 0°C or above. This freezing point then becomes the boiling point, also known as the Celsius point (100°C = 273.8°F).
When the freezing point of pure water drops below this temperature, it begins to boil. At this point, the liquid turns into vapour (liquid water) and rises up through the atmosphere to become fog, mist or rain.
If you were to get out of bed for an hour without drinking anything, you would be able to feel your body warming itself by sweating out the heat. But if you are exposed to air with temperatures lower than 0°C, your body will turn into steam, not water!
You can see that water has a higher boiling point than any other substance, so we have used it to describe things like lava, salt, oil, etc. It is very important to remember that water has many different properties and is not all equally cold or hot; it does not necessarily mean that it is cold or hot.

The art of the day was created in 1853 by Charles Willson Peale. The work is a portrait of Abraham Lincoln from his early days as a slave and later as president. This picture shows Lincoln as a man who is educated and with dignity as he sits on the ground next to an abolitionist in front of the crowd at the Lincoln Memorial. It also depicts Lincoln looking into the Lincoln Gallery where many slaves were held. These pictures are one of only four portraits of President Abraham Lincoln that have survived.
In 2014, there were two portraits of Mr. Lincoln in the collection of the Library of Congress. One is from 1975 and the other was dated July 2, 1976. Both photos show a small child playing with his favorite toy. They have been restored by the museum.
